question: Which private-equity rivals are most active in our sectors?
html:
Residential services, where Punctual Pros operates, has the most active rivals. Apex (Alpine), Wrench (LGP) and, in PA/NJ, Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy/HL Bowman (Gridiron) and Ally (Watchtower) are buying near Punctual Pros. In CET's electrical market, Kohlberg and Huron are the active sponsors, but mostly outside New England (Private-equity landscape).

Activity by sector

Sector (portfolio company)Most active rivalsRead
Residential HVAC/plumbing (Punctual Pros)Apex/Alpine, Wrench/LGP, TurnPoint/OMERS, Redwood/Altas, Any Hour/Knox Lane, T3/Riverside. Locally: Sila, Legacy/HL Bowman, Ally, Northwinds (TruArc)Most crowded. National consolidators set add-on pricing
Electrical and energy services (CET)Kohlberg (RESA Power, Loenbro, CLEAResult); Huron (Criticore, Albireo)Gap in New England. Watch Albireo's Upstate NY expansion
Legal IT and billing services (Frontline)Alpine's Evergreen, EagleTree/Integreon, BVNo direct sponsor-backed copy yet
Lab distribution (Thomas Scientific)Calibre ScientificMain bidder for U.S. add-ons, but focused on Europe

Pace and financial strength

  • Apex completed 46 add-ons in 2023 and 60 in 2025 (Home-services company case studies).
  • Sila's growth has come almost entirely from acquisitions. Its revenue is est. $450–650M, a low-confidence estimate (Competitor filings).
  • Several rivals are under financial strain. Horizon pays 3.75% PIK interest, is marked at 92.5 and is lender-owned by 2026. Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026. Both are more likely to sell assets than to bid (Competitor filings).
  • IES is a public strategic buyer, not PE. It has no net debt and 11.4% operating margins, so it can pay strategic prices for New England contractors (Competitor filings).

Firm-level peers

  • The closest thesis peers are MidOcean, CIVC, Trilantic North America, Palladium, Vesterra/Comvest and Bertram (Private-equity landscape).
  • Fund sizes are uneven:
  • BSP Fund I is about $335M.
  • Trivest VII is $950M.
  • Bertram V and MidOcean VI are $1.5B each.
  • Gridiron V is $2.1B.
  • Gridiron backs Legacy/HL Bowman and is the largest fund buying near Punctual Pros.

Gaps and caveats

  • There is no rival-sponsor data for BPI or Fair Harbor. Answering that would need deal-flow data for strategic-communications and DTC apparel deals.
  • Research ran out of web-search quota partway through. Some fund sizes are unknown, including Trilantic VII and Palladium VI (Private-equity landscape).
  • Rival leverage and EBITDA figures are analyst estimates based on one lender's view of each loan.

Next actions

  1. Punctual Pros: Build a proprietary outreach list of sub-$3M EBITDA shops in Central PA/NJ. Lead with Authority Brands territory rights and brand conversion rather than joining auctions.
  2. Punctual Pros: Watch the Horizon and Heartland situations ahead of Dec 15, 2026, and prepare for possible asset sales.
  3. CET: Speed up New England add-ons before Albireo or Kohlberg's energy-efficiency group reaches the region.
  4. BPI and Fair Harbor: Commission a rival-sponsor scan to fill the data gap.
